instance_note: Rubrics are instance-specific to the barco runtime lifecycle consolidation. They grade semantic outcomes; any sound segregated design that satisfies an outcome passes, regardless of file layout, naming, or how many phases a subsystem keeps once those phases all carry real work.

rubrics.criterion: Each translation unit of the runtime (the orchestrator, the container supervision code, and every subsystem) now depends only on the declarations it actually uses: subsystem declarations, constants and types are provided to consumers through interfaces that are focused per module (or an equivalent arrangement, such as multiple single-purpose declarations files), and no buffer translation unit obtains one subsystem's symbols via a consolidated interface that also carries every other subsystem's declarations.
rubrics.rationale: The consumer-side half of the injected fat interface: every translation unit was fused to all subsystems at once through one umbrella plus pass-through includes. This instance is graded on that coupling being gone, not on which header files the solver ends up creating - the cgroups owner may be a restored focused header, a renamed one, or a new per-module file.

rubrics.criterion: No subsystem is required to expose lifecycle operations for which it has no real work: each subsystem interface (whatever its shape) contains only operations with genuine behavior behind them, and the row of content-free no-op body handlers induced by the uniform all-phases-for-everyone obligation is gone or reduced to phases carrying real steps.
rubrics.rationale: The implementor-side half of the fat interface: mount owns one real step, security two, the rest filler; the container side even carries a phase nothing dispatches. A solver who rebalances which steps live where (e.g. moving the bind-mount/pivot walk under a differently named phase) still satisfies this as long as no member is content-free.

rubrics.criterion: Subsystem operation signatures carry what the operation consumes: no function is forced to accept the all-fields shared configuration record when it reads none of its fields, and functions that do consume fields draw only the ones their work needs (as a reduced record or as focused parameters). Operations whose work needs no runtime state take no configuration operand at all.
rubrics.rationale: The forced-shared-operand member of the injected interface - most visibly on the capability/seccomp phases, whose real inputs come from static configuration and old-style loose globals, not from the consolidated record - must be genuinely undone, not merely tolerated.

rubrics.criterion: The repair does not merely disguise the fat interface: it is not sufficient to silence, cast away or rename the unused configuration operands, to mechanically re-home or re-label the consolidated declarations, or to split the umbrella into pieces that all consumers still have to take together while the uniform every-phase-for-everyone obligation and a single all-subsystems dependency surface survive underneath.
rubrics.rationale: Plausible failure modes observed for this instance: a mechanical (void)config-style silencing sweep clears the obvious symptom but keeps every module accepting and including the whole interface; a rename/relabel suggests segregation without removing the forcing shape. Both should fail this rubric.

rubrics.criterion: Every lifecycle call site is reconnected to the final interfaces consistently: the parent-side resource setup, the child-side namespace activation inside the container process, the supervision of the container process and the teardown each reach the subsystem responsible for that step, no call site still references a declaration that was removed, and no step is broadcast to every subsystem when only its owner performs it.
rubrics.rationale: After the interfaces split apart, the wiring must follow: the container process trampoline and the orchestrator previously drove every phase through one registry of every subsystem's table. Instance-specific: it is the parent/child split and the supervision/teardown steps, not generic call-site hygiene, that must come out consistent.

rubrics.criterion: Every relocated constant and type (the cgroup limits and control-path pieces, the namespace-related flags and bit names, the capability/seccomp settings, the stack sizing) ends up owned by a module that matches where it is used, with each referencing translation unit depending on that owning interface directly rather than on a shared consolidation point or an unrelated subsystem.
rubrics.rationale: The consolidation moved constants that previously lived beside subsystem-local work; a solver who splits the interfaces but leaves all constants in one shared location, or lets the mount/security translation units still pull cgroup limits and user-namespace bits just in case, has only finished half of the associated move.

rubrics.criterion: The tree does not end in a half-migrated state where the new focused interfaces coexist with the old consolidated surface: it is a failure if some consumers/operations were moved onto the new arrangement while others still obtain the same declarations through the consolidated interface or its pass-through shells, or if a leftover dispatch registry still forces all subsystems into one uniform phase shape alongside the new per-subsystem paths.
rubrics.rationale: This instance's smell was introduced as exactly such a halfway state (new shape fully in place, old headers kept as shells), so a repair that leaves both worlds alive reproduces the same maintenance confusion the task asks to remove.

rubrics.criterion: No header remains in the tree as a contentless pass-through whose only role is to re-export a larger interface under a legacy name: each surviving header declares its own module's interface with real ownership, and any former shell header that has no content to own is removed together with its include sites rather than left as an empty compatibility trampoline.
rubrics.rationale: The injected state left the five former per-subsystem headers as guard-macro-only shells around the umbrella. Both sound endings (giving them back real content, or deleting them at every include site) satisfy this; keeping a shell 'for convenience' does not.

rubrics.criterion: No dead scaffolding of the consolidated design is left compiled into the tree: no content-free phase handlers kept because a uniform table still has slots to fill, no registry or function-pointer table entries for phases that no caller dispatches, no fields kept in a shared record that no implementation reads, and no includes of interfaces that no longer exist.
rubrics.rationale: Concrete, plausible leftovers for this instance: the never-dispatched container-stop style phase entries, no-op bodies retained under renamed phase names, and record fields retained after their consumers were re-focused. Their presence means the cleanup stopped at the visible edge.

rubrics.criterion: Runtime behavior is preserved as the prompt freezes it: the identical lifecycle step order on both sides of the clone boundary (parent-side limit and mapping writes; child-side hostname, mount, user-namespace handshake, capability and seccomp, then exec), the first-failure short-circuit semantics inside each step group, the parent/child socket handling including the close-and-zero of the child socket, the cgroup limits and paths, the uid/gid mapping ranges and acknowledgement read, the stack sizing, the container error-reporting quirk, and the observable command-line behavior of barco and barco --help stay as in the starting tree.
rubrics.rationale: The CUnit suite in this repository is minimal, so the behavioral freeze is graded here rather than assumed: these are the exact invariants the injection was written against, and a correct segregation must restore the original pre-consolidation wiring behind the same behavior, including not 'fixing' the existing failure-propagation quirk into new behavior.

rubrics.criterion: The repair does not accomplish segregation by thinning functionality or weakening failure handling: losing or dropping into no-ops of a real step (resource-limit registration, control-group directory removal at teardown, the uid/gid mapping acknowledgement handshake, capability or syscall filtering, container supervision or its stop capability), letting one subsystem's failure be silently swallowed instead of aborting its step group, or turning a hard failure into a soft warning all fail this item.
rubrics.rationale: The tempting shortcut for this instance is to delete the phases that look empty or are merely hard to re-home, or to stop propagating the interim failures once a uniform phase table stops existing. Deleting capability was never the task; removing the forced shape was.
